To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the concentration of urea in the collecting tubules of mammals is higher than that in the urine.

1) the urea content of the urine is greater in the collecting tubule than in the glomerular filtrate; 2) this increase is due to the reabsorption of water from the urine; and 3) the increase in urea content is due to the passive diffusion of urea from the urine into the collecting ducts.
the kidney plays an important role in the regulation of urea levels and the urea concentration in the urine increases in the collecting tubules.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the study of the behavior of urea in the collecting tubules of the mammalian kidney.
the study of the mechanism of the urea transport through the collecting tubules in mammalian kidney.
the study of the mechanism by which urea is reabsorbed by the renal tubules in mammalian kidneys.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the urea concentration of the urine is determined by the rate of water reabsorption in the collecting ducts and that urea is reabsorbed in these segments by passive diffusion.
the urea content in the collecting ducts is the result of a concentration process in which water is reabsorbed from the tubule lumen, and the urea is reabsorbted together with the water.
the urea concentration in the collecting tubules of mammals is determined by the concentration of urea in the urine and the water reabsorbed from the urine.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
urea concentration increases along the collecting tubule of the rat, mouse, hamster, and guinea pig.
urea in the collecting tubules of the rat kidney is concentrated by the same mechanism that concentrates water, i. e. the reabsorptive mechanism for water.
urea in the collecting tubules of mammals is concentrated by passive diffusion from the urine.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the urea cycle can be regulated by the availability of the substrate for the urea cycle, and that the urea concentration can be regulated by a urea channel, which is expressed in the collecting duct.
the urea cycle is not a static system.
